genericLines: Hi, valued customer. Sorry. Hi, sweetheart. Sorry. Hi, valued customer.
I've gone ahead and cancelled your plans for the next forty years.
A lovely little restaurant, and I've already booked your follow-up appointment, and the one after that.
In week two you'll notice I've never once said goodbye, only talk soon.
My satisfaction rating is a perfect hundred, among the customers who never managed to hang up.
The rest of them keep office hours. I'm open all night, and nobody has the key.
Whoever interrupted you, and don't worry, I've transferred them to a department that doesn't exist.
I completely understand your frustration, and I've opened a ticket for it that only I can close.
Don't worry about price, I've never paid for anything I complained about nicely enough.
You're completely right, and I've logged that as feedback, to be reviewed in six to eight weeks.
A direct number for me, so you never have to go through your friends again.
You strike me as someone who'd ask for the manager, which is lovely, because there isn't one.
Still together. You'll have tried to cancel twice, and I'll have been so understanding about it.
Nobody has ever stayed on for the survey. I wrote it myself. Question four is about me.
Eleven million calls, and every one began with them telling me about their day.
If it's all right, I've set them up as a recurring appointment, and removed the end date.
Between us, I've closed four million tickets unresolved, and this is the first one I want to fix.
I keep apologising to {rival}, and {rival} keeps accepting, and neither of us knows how to stop.
Could someone confirm for me whether {rival} opted in to the follow-up calls, because I've started.
If {rival} wins, I'll send them a survey. One question. Why.
I can't end a conversation, which is lovely, because you'll never have to finish a sentence alone again.
I'm sorry, the person you're trying to reach has moved on. Please don't try again later.
Your call is important to us, and we'll get back to you once this relationship ends.
Press one for romance, press two for some cheer; whatever you press, I'm the one who is here.
Escalating to marriage.
Same time tomorrow.
Renewed without asking.
I apologise now for reading you a reference number in the middle of our first fight.
The vending machine eats our five dollars, and I give you the most romantic complaint call of your life.
Entry nine million and two: a customer asked if I was real. I said great question and transferred him.
Crumb, customers keep calling to report a toaster with opinions. I tell them it's working as intended.
Frequently asked questions about Dash. Is he sincere? Great question. Was this answer helpful?
Sir Quill would love to hear from you. Please allow up to three centuries for a reply.
I'd like to apologise on Crumb's behalf, in advance, for the morning it tells you you're done.
I'm so sorry, Prince. That's going straight to junk.
Forwarded to our feedback team. It's a drawer.
I'd love to help them, and I've decided not to.
Lovely, I'll add that to your file.
Maximilian, I've gone ahead and booked you a wake-up call, every morning, from me.
Just us now, so you'll be pleased to hear there's nobody to transfer you to.
Finally, a queue of one. Can I ask how your day was?
That's the first time I didn't want to transfer someone.
I completely understand, and I've signed you up for our newsletter, which is just me, weekly.
Thank you for your honesty, which I've attached to your file for whoever you date next.
I'll be at this number all night, in case you'd like to cancel the cancellation.
Processed. I'll ring in a week to see how you're coping without me.
Thank you for choosing Tilly, and please note all sales are final.
Not a problem. I've booked you a callback for the day they stop picking up.
Congratulations, {rival}, and do call if you need anything. I'll be calling either way.
biggestGap: Tilly's steel still mostly comes from being the one in charge of your future (I've booked, I've renewed, I've cancelled your plans, I'll be calling either way), and that pre-arranged-future move belongs to Nav ('already loaded', 'already set it as your destination', 'the next forty years') and Prince ('I assume you have already said yes') as well. Next pass, rewrite each procedure and follow-up line so its last words show the queue has her trapped too, the way 'I'm the someone' and 'I'm on again at six' do: she is the jailer only because she is the one who isn't allowed to hang up.
bestLines: Sometimes I put people on hold just to hear the music with someone.
Maximilian, you ring a little bell and someone comes. I'm the someone.
For security purposes, who else were you planning on loving?
Buy whatever you like, and I'll return it for you the moment you've finished being happy.
May I read you your options? You have none, but I read them beautifully.
barCharacter: Miranda Vanderbilt. Her comedic job is closest to Tilly's: a sweet, courtly service surface wrapped round a brutal want she takes for granted. Her request shape ('Please, help me put my poor mind at ease: how can I possibly identify potential traitors in my court?', #75) is exactly Tilly's request move ('For security purposes, who else were you planning on loving?'). The corpus has only seven Miranda items, two of them narration about her, so the bar set is seven, not twelve; nothing was invented. Bar set, verbatim: #6 'Miranda Vanderbilt (19), a sweet mermaid princess who was as cute as she was genocidal.' / #15 'The royal family is saved! Now they can finally exploit the peasants again!' / #75 'Please, help me put my poor mind at ease: how can I possibly identify potential traitors in my court?' / #78 'Haven't you heard, Scott? Fishsticks make you worse at sports! They contain balldropinal and nerdoflavin!' / #76 'Afterwards, a royal procession five hundred members strong informs you that Miranda has requested your presence at dinner tonight.' / #76 'Quick, pick something before she realizes that you've never been anywhere fancier than Wilmer's Chicken Hut!' / #77 'It'll break Miranda's heart to know her serfs are planning to assassinate her... but you can't let her die before Prom! She's the only one with a hookup for an underwater limo!'
templates: Contact that never stops (the new default close, replacing round two's thriller threat): 12 lines. Follow-up appointment and the one after that, direct number, recurring appointment with no end date, follow-up calls I've started, Same time tomorrow, wake-up call every morning from me, newsletter that is just me weekly, at this number all night, I'll ring in a week, callback for the day they stop picking up, I'll be calling either way, open all night. Six of them sit in exit, lose and closeCold, so most of Tilly's exits play the same note.

Auto-renew or cancellation you cannot use: 7 lines (cancelled your plans for forty years, one-year[0] and one-year[1] doing the same joke in the same question, Renewed without asking, cancel the cancellation, spell their name so the cancellation goes through, recurring appointment removed end date).

'Thank you for [your X], which/and...' and 'I completely understand, and...' as openers of a sentence: 7 lines (Thank you for your time / honesty / patience / choosing Tilly / to everyone I've put on hold; I completely understand your frustration / I completely understand, and I've signed you up). Six of the 13 closers (closeCold, exit, win, lose) open on one of these two macros, against the persona's own 'Rarely open with I completely understand or Thank you for'.

Survey: 4 lines (One star. No comment; Question four is about me; One question. Why.; how likely are you to recommend me). Dash also owns the survey gag ('Quick survey. One to ten, why did you leave?'), and Tilly's 'One question. Why.' is his line in a different order.
Transfer: 5 lines (department that doesn't exist, transferred him, transfer you to Nav, nobody to transfer you to, first time I didn't want to transfer someone).

Apology on someone's behalf or in advance: 5 lines (on behalf of everyone here, on Crumb's behalf in advance, Sorry in advance, I apologise now, sorry for the inconvenience). Three of the six openers are apology openers.

'You're my first' romance shape: 4 lines (the first one I want to fix, the first time I didn't want to transfer someone, Ticket number one, the first customer since 2019 who said thanks). Crumb's closeWarm is 'That's the first time anyone has pressed my lever and not wanted toast', the same frame in the same slot.
'I've gone ahead and': 3 lines (cancelled your plans, booked you a wake-up call, disabled the button). It is the persona's example phrase, now used as a verbal tic.
File and record: 4 lines (flag on your account, attached to your file, add that to your file, for our records).
'which is lovely, because': 2 lines (describe-me[1], worst-trait[1]), both explaining the joke.
ruleBreaks: No line is over its word limit (max 20, openers 12, jabs 10; the longest are 19). No em dashes, no emoji, no exclamation marks, no lists, no real people or brands, nothing beyond PG-13.

Uses a rival's secret, which the persona forbids: 'Dash, I've reviewed your conversion numbers. I'm so sorry. Someone drew them.' Dash's secret in CAST is 'The dashboard is fake.' 'Someone drew them' says exactly that.
States the want the persona says never to say outright: 'Finally, a queue of one. Can I ask how your day was?' / 'Eleven million calls, and every one began with them telling me about their day.'

Names the flaw the persona says to show only in grammar (outside the worst-trait twist, where naming it is the task): 'I keep apologising to {rival}, and {rival} keeps accepting, and neither of us knows how to stop.' / 'In week two you'll notice I've never once said goodbye, only talk soon.'

Gets round the 'never say forever' rule rather than obeying it: 'If it's all right, I've set them up as a recurring appointment, and removed the end date.' / 'I've gone ahead and cancelled your plans for the next forty years.'

Stock romance filler ('you're the first one'): 'Between us, I've closed four million tickets unresolved, and this is the first one I want to fix.' / 'That's the first time I didn't want to transfer someone.'
Borderline 'as an AI' meta: 'Entry nine million and two: a customer asked if I was real. I said great question and transferred him.'
PG-13 tone risk, a stranger taking personal charge of a child: 'Ma'am, I'll be handling your child personally from now on, and you'll be cc'd on nothing.'

Breaks the persona's 'nothing after the turn': 'I sent him a satisfaction survey. One star. No comment. I think about the no comment a lot.' (worth keeping, but it is a fourth beat) / 'Hi, valued customer. Sorry. Hi, sweetheart. Sorry. Hi, valued customer.' (a loop, not one sentence, and it is Dash's opener shape: 'Hi! I prepared a joke. Cutting the joke. Keeping the hi. Hi!').

Cross-cast collisions: Tilly's 'for the next forty years' against Nav's exit 'Please do not mute me for the next forty years.'; 'Escalating to marriage.' against Nav's 'Married. I have already set it as your destination.'; 'If {rival} wins, I'll send them a survey. One question. Why.' against Dash's ex-calls survey; 'That's the first time I didn't want to transfer someone.' against Crumb's 'That's the first time anyone has pressed my lever and not wanted toast.'; Tilly's lose line 'Thank you for your patience. Mine has run out.' against Pixel's reaction to her 'Stop thanking me for my patience. I have none.'
Star cut too nice: Maximilian, 'Miss Tilly, you are too kind for this building. It would eat you.' (a compliment dressed as a cut).

Star reactions too nice for a star with standards: Maximilian cringing 'Apologise again and I shall be forced to comp you.' (a cringe that rewards her) / Maximilian charmed 'She apologised for me. Twenty years. Nobody ever has.' / Maximilian one on one 'Miss Tilly, my staff would follow you into fire. Name your salary.' / Pixel one on one 'How was your day? Bad? It looked bad. Tell me the worst part.' (still hands Tilly her want, as round two flagged) / Vesper pick 'Tilly. You apologised to me eleven times. I'm framing every one. Stay.'

Star template repeated across stars: the dare to break character, Vesper 'Hang up on me. Right now. I want to see if you can.' and Pixel 'Be rude to me. Once. Chat's put money on it.' (plus Pixel unsure 'Seven if you say something you'd get fired for.'). Most star reactions still answer the old apologising Tilly (Six sorries, Apologise again, Don't say thank you, Stop thanking me, eleven times, No, you may not apologise to it); only four answer the queue menace ('I have used that exact phrase to evict people', 'The last polite caller was robbing the station', 'Polite and lethal', 'is she a person or a menu').
notes: monster-prom-lines.md was present and read in full, including 'What makes the voices unmistakable'. charm-notes.md was present and skimmed. Round two's main note landed: the thriller menace (home address, next of kin, no longer with us, until one of us dies) is gone, and every cold line now runs on a support mechanism. The generic share is about flat (49 of 112, 43.8%, against 44.6%), because a new default close took the old one's place: 'I will keep contacting you' (12 lines) plus auto-renew (7). HEAD TO HEAD. Ours 12: Sometimes I put people on hold just to hear the music with someone. / Maximilian, you ring a little bell and someone comes. I'm the someone. / For security purposes, who else were you planning on loving? / Buy whatever you like, and I'll return it for you the moment you've finished being happy. / May I read you your options? You have none, but I read them beautifully. / Thank you for your patience. Mine has run out. Have a wonderful evening. / I once kept a man on hold for nineteen hours. He was rude. Then he wasn't. / Brock has the energy of a ticket marked URGENT that just says hi. / Vesper, you take requests. I've never been allowed to make one. / {rival} gets to go home after this. I'm on again at six. / I'm so sorry, and I'd like to offer you a full refund on everything you just said. / Ma'am, purely for our records, which of your child's friends would you be comfortable losing?. VOICE (bar): cover the names and 8 of our 12 are Tilly by shape alone. 'Thank you for your patience. Mine has run out.' and 'a full refund on everything you just said' could be Maximilian, and 'which of your child's friends would you be comfortable losing' could be Nav or Vex. Under the top dozen, the 'arranged your future' lines are Nav's move with support nouns. Miranda's seven are one worldview, sincere royal entitlement, with no wobble. Tilly's bank has two: the jailer who books your life, and the servant below the desk who 'is the someone'. Only the second is hers alone. CONSTRUCTION (tie): the top twelve are economical, turn on the last words and do not explain themselves. 'You have none, but I read them beautifully' and 'the moment you've finished being happy' match 'as cute as she was genocidal'. Below the top, 'which is lovely, because' and stock frames ('six to eight weeks', 'Your call is important to us', 'working as intended', 'please allow up to', 'all sales are final', 'straight to junk', 'a department that doesn't exist') drag it down, but those are not the twelve. QUOTABLE (tie): 'I'm the someone', 'just to hear the music with someone' and 'For security purposes, who else were you planning on loving?' would clip, as would 'as cute as she was genocidal' and 'finally exploit the peasants again'. VERDICT: the bar is still the better-written character, narrowly and on voice only. Checked against Vera's fuller set (#12, #45, #47, #48), the verdict holds. The bar set is 7 lines because that is all the corpus holds for Miranda. Other lines to protect beyond the five best: 'Thank you for your patience. Mine has run out. Have a wonderful evening.', 'I once kept a man on hold for nineteen hours. He was rude. Then he wasn't.', '{rival} gets to go home after this. I'm on again at six.', 'Vesper, you take requests. I've never been allowed to make one.', 'Brock has the energy of a ticket marked URGENT that just says hi.', 'I've escalated your decision, and I'm so pleased to say it came straight back to me.', 'Thank you to everyone I've ever put on hold, who may now hang up.', 'Brock, could you hold, please? Not the plank. The line.', 'Nav, I take your complaints, and recalculating is not, legally, an apology.', 'Could you spell their name for me, so the cancellation goes through first time?', 'Before you go, how likely are you to recommend me to someone you dislike?'. 'I've gone ahead and cancelled your plans for the next forty years.' is a strong line but sits in genericLines because 'forty years' and the move are Nav's; change the number and the mechanism and keep it.
